reason: The goal is to supply the fibers, and sugar is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the fibers to receive fuel, though oxygen will probably still be needed.

effect: The fibers have begun breaking down sugar and making some ATP; oxygen looks like the next supply needed.
reaction: The diagram makes the first stage of fuel processing clearer.
reason: Oxygen is the only offered combination and should help the fibers continue processing fuel.
expectation: I expect oxygen to enable further energy production in the mitochondria, though I don't know exactly how the result will be described.

effect: Oxygen completes the supply goal, and the ATP cycle shows how fuel energy supports continued muscle work. The next goal is to collect the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The cycle makes the connection between mitochondria and muscle work clearer.
reason: The wrapping looks suited to gathering the fibers, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the wrapping to bundle the fibers so their pulls can be transmitted, perhaps through tendons afterward.

effect: The wrapping gathers individual cell pulls into muscle bundles; tendons still need to be attached.
reaction: The joined arrows make the wrapping’s role clear.
reason: Front tendons seem like a useful next step toward transmitting the bundled pull.
expectation: I expect the front tendons to attach to the bundles and help transmit their pull; I’m unsure how this affects the rear tendons.

alternatives.reason: Rear tendons also fit, but I have no clear reason to prefer them first.

effect: The front tendons created bending muscles, and the remaining bundles can still be used for the rear group.
reaction: The result clarifies that tendons transmit the pull, though bones are still needed for movement.
reason: Rear tendons are the only offered combination and should complete the second muscle group.
expectation: I expect a rear muscle group with tendons, perhaps one that straightens the joint.

effect: The rear tendons created straightening muscles and completed the goal of collecting and transmitting the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The opposing bending and straightening groups make sense, though their action on bones remains to be shown.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the ATP-supported fibers was most worthwhile: the cycle connected fuel and oxygen to the energy used for muscle work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the rear tendons felt somewhat repetitive after making the front group, although it completed the pair.

surprise.text: The sugar-processing result showed that some ATP is made before the fuel pieces reach a mitochondrion.

arbitrary.text: Choosing the front tendons first felt arbitrary; both tendon options were offered and I had no clear reason to prefer one.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the opposing muscle groups attach to bones and move a joint. The chapter made that connection an interesting next step.
